image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on blue water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow-green bill, and a mottled brown and grey body. It is positioned in the center of the frame, facing slightly left, with its reflection visible in the rippling water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and exhibits the correct yellow-green coloration typical of a male mallard.
The eye is visible against the dark green head plumage and appears dark/black as expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing buoyant and streamlined. The plumage texture looks dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic male mallard pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; the legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The folded wings are visible along the side of the body, showing appropriate breadth and tapering towards the tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear of the bird, appearing short and exhibiting the slight upward curl characteristic of drakes.
